issue_context.title: Should the function `AreLabelsInWhiteList` return false when the whitelist is empty?
comments:
/assign @lavalamp 
/cc @liggitt 
(we think you might have opinions on fixing this)
I only see one consumer.  Rather than change the semantic, I would suggest moving it to the point of use and renaming it.

Yes, this function is wrong, I agree with David.

P.S. we don't advertise interface stability for this library so this is OK. But even if we did, I think callers of this function are probably not expecting this behavior and should be examined.)

P.P.S. The way it should work is via set difference, the labels should be a subset of the list.

P.P.P.S. These are sets and not lists, and the names should be changed to reflect that.

P.P.P.P.S. If you're making a change here anyway, please lose the word "whitelist".
Okay,  I will submit a pr.

review_comments: please remove the original.  I don't think we need it anymore and that's a clear signal to everyone they should re-examine their code.
